sections.history: Ujjain, the Avantika of old, is one of the seven sacred cities of India, and the Dvadasha Jyotirlinga Stotram names "Mahakala in Ujjayini" among the twelve Jyotirlingas. The poet Kalidasa wrote of the shrine of Mahakala and its evening worship, and the temple flourished under the Paramara kings. In the raid of the Delhi sultan Iltutmish in 1234–35 it was laid waste; tradition holds that the linga was kept safe in the temple tank, Koti Tirtha. The present temple was raised around 1734 under the Maratha commander Ranoji Shinde, whose diwan Ramchandra Baba Shenvi carried out the work, and the Scindia rulers of Gwalior long remained its patrons. In 2022 the broad Shri Mahakal Lok precinct was opened around the temple.
sections.architecture: The temple rises in three storeys above a deep sanctum. On the lowest level, reached by steps below the courtyard, is Mahakaleshwar himself; above him is a shrine of Omkareshwar, and at the top a shrine of Nagachandreshwar, Shiva and Parvati seated on a many-hooded serpent, opened to devotees only on Nag Panchami. The linga faces south, the direction of Yama, so Mahakala is worshipped as Dakshinamurti, master of death and time. The Koti Tirtha tank lies within the precinct, ringed by smaller shrines.
sections.legends: The Shiva Purana tells that the demon Dushana, armed with a boon of Brahma, tormented the devout of Avantika and above all the family of the Brahmin Vedapriya, who kept up their worship of an earthen linga. As the demon advanced, the ground split open and Shiva burst forth as Mahakala, reducing him to ash with a single roar. At the devotees' plea he remained in that place as a Jyotirlinga, guardian of the city. Another story tells of King Chandrasena and a cowherd boy, Shrikar, whose simple devotion was rewarded with Shiva's presence.
sections.festivals: Each day begins with the Bhasma Aarti before dawn, when the linga is worshipped with sacred ash. Maha Shivaratri is preceded by nine days of festival worship, and on Mondays through Shravan and Bhadrapada the festival image of Mahakal is borne in a palanquin through the city in the Sawari procession. Once every twelve years the Simhastha Kumbh Mela gathers millions on the Shipra. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: The Bhasma Aarti is the experience most pilgrims seek: the hush before dawn, the bells and drums, and the linga dressed in ash as the chants rise. It must be booked in advance and carries its own dress rules. Later in the day, darshan moves through the long queues of the Mahakal Lok, and the ghats of the Shipra and the Harsiddhi temple are a short walk away.

visit.timings: Open daily from before dawn until late night, beginning with the Bhasma Aarti; confirm timings and aarti booking locally, as arrangements change on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected; for the Bhasma Aarti, men are asked to wear a dhoti and women a saree. Footwear is removed before entering.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted in the sanctum; follow posted rules and staff guidance in the corridor and courtyards.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in the old city of Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, about 2 km from Ujjain Junction railway station. The nearest airport is Indore, about 55 km away by road.
